pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/13424

Some `ReplayFrame`s now come with a `FrameHeader` themselves. For spectator, the last frame in each bundle contains the relevant score data up to that point in time. This special frame is used to reset the `ScoreProcessor` into the correct state, updating two important variables:
1. `JudgedHits`, which allows spectator to now always transition to the results screen regardless of where spectator started. This is particularly noticeable if you started spectating in the middle of gameplay, where the spectating client doesn't have knowledge about all previous judgements.
2. `TotalScore`, `Accuracy`, et al. Now spectator always shows the correct info at all points in time.

The header isn't serialised as part of the frame - it gets injected into the last frame when the bundle arrives at the spectating client. I would have liked to add in special intermediate frames rather than bundling the header into `ReplayFrame`, however this seems like a non-trivial task due to the implementation of `FramedReplayInputHandler` casting everything and using floating indices for retrieving the Previous/Current/Start/End frames.

Note that this does not fi(x) https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/14768, which I believe is a result of _both_ this issue and a multitude of other issues relating to the playing state. I have a WIP branch fixing this, but it's a completely separate change.

There are two caveats to this implementation:
1. `ScoreProcessor` now has to serialise all judgement data, which now includes `IgnoreHit` and `IgnoreMiss` judgements. I believe this is what we want anyway as it's quite hard to calculate scores otherwise.
2. The `ScoreProcessor` implementation doesn't support multiple hitobjects having different maximum judgements. For example, if one hitobject in a ruleset has `MaxResult = GREAT`, then _all_ hitobjects of that ruleset must have `MaxResult = GREAT`. This doesn't apply to ticks/bonus. I don't know if there's an amicable way to resolve this until we start serialising more data about the score (judgement + hitobject index, maybe) which can be considered in the future. I don't think this is a bad limitation for the time being.

This does not require any osu-server-spectator changes/deploy.

# Breaking changes

## `FramedReplayInputHandler.CollectPendingInputs` renamed to `FramedReplayHandler.CollectReplayInputs`

Accessibility has also changed from `public` to `protected`, however the rest of the method signature remains identical and a simple find-replace can be used to fix existing usages.
pr_comments: Seems like the breaking change could potentially be obsoleted (renaming the base method to something else so we can still maintain the new flow) - is that not something we want to do?
Oh wow... it's a framework level method..
